messages:
julia: quick thought experiment: what if we "slim" API surface by making most keys implicit — only mint short-lived intent tokens for calls. want quick takes before i write an RFC.

mike: sounds good. main tension i see is mint latency vs avoiding long-lived creds. can we cache minted tokens at the edge?

sarah: caching helps but TTLs need to be clear. short TTLs = safer but more mint ops. also need a clear parent->child lineage for audit.

cory: ops: mint service adds a critical path. we need throttles and a deterministic fallback if mint is down (deny vs derived-claims?).

julia: proposal: precedence = minted token -> cached derived claims -> deny. derived-claims are only allowed for low-risk read routes. write paths require minted tokens.

alexa: for billing/audit, include `parent` claim in minted token. avoid adding token ids to metrics to keep cardinality low (use org/project/principal-type).

mike: agree on metrics. we should track shadow-mint rate and lineage-loss rate.

sarah: RBAC: map claims into existing static role ids in policy engine. no per-token dynamic roles. simpler for audits.

cory: migration: accept legacy long-lived keys for a window, shadow-mint and emit deprecation telemetry, then reduce privileges.

deploy-bot: canary started for token-slimmer experiment: https://deploys.internal/redwood/rollouts/3400

julia: thanks. i'll draft RFC with token shapes, claim vocab, fallback circuit, migration plan, and SLOs. owners: julia RFC lead, cory ops, mike telemetry, sarah policy, alexa docs. target in two weeks.
